rationale: These seven files were picked because they carry the shapes that made TypeScript the worst-covered of the eight languages: against the pre-ATL-096 walker they measure 0.486 / 0.217, close to the 0.229 / 0.085 the whole 53-file repo scored. constants.ts opens with a module-scope IIFE containing an object getter, delay.ts nests `function abortHandler()` inside a callback, body.ts and http-error.ts pass object-literal methods to `new TransformStream({transform() {}})` / `new ReadableStream({start() {}})`, and headers.ts assigns a named class expression to `globalThis.Headers`. READ THIS BEFORE ASSUMING named_funcs IS A BUG. 0.514 is a decision, not a miss: 36 of the fixture's 70 method_definitions (179 of 223 across the whole repo) hang off an object literal in argument position or an inline return, and this walker declines them. ADR-0031's test is whether a developer has a name for the thing, and the grammar node's spelling is not that test — `ky(url, {async fetch() {...}})` produces a `method_definition`, but the method belongs to an anonymous inline object and nothing can refer to it, so it is a callback exactly like the arrow it could have been written as. An object-literal method becomes an entity only when its object is itself bound (a const/let/var, a class field, or a property chain that reaches one), and is then named through that binding: `handlers.fetch`. The proof that this is a naming decision rather than a walker hole is that `calls` did not move: declining the entity relocates its calls to the enclosing named scope, it does not lose them. tests/support/langcov.py counts every method_definition as named, so this ratio cannot reach 1.0 while that classification and this rule disagree; 0.51 is still a tight ratchet, since losing a single captured form drops it to 0.500. The 0.4% call shortfall is 5 nodes of 1208, each naming nothing a graph could point at — 3 IIFEs `(() => {...})()`, whose callee is the arrow literal itself; 1 `super(...)`, already recorded as the class's INHERITS edge; and 1 `response[type]()`, a computed member resolved at runtime. Repo-wide the same kinds account for 16 of 6508 (0.25%), adding curried `promisify(fn)()` and dynamic `import('...')`, a module specifier rather than a callable. max_duplicate_uids is 10 and none of them is an object method: they are repeated `const customFetch = async () => {...}` locals declared inside sibling anonymous `test(...)` callbacks in http-error.ts (8) and headers.ts (4). Those are bound to a const, so ADR-0031 category 2 makes them entities, but the only scope that can qualify them is the module — the callback between them has no name, and a positional one is banned. ky's source/ tree has 0 duplicates; the full 53-file checkout has 57, all of this same shape, all in test/.
